oewn-01726584-s.learner: not able to be shown to be right, or not able to be explained.
examples: The judge called the harsh sentence insupportable, since nothing could justify it.

connotation.why: condemns a claim or act as having no defence, against plain 'unexplained'

oewn-14604877-n.learner: the solid stuff that a physical thing is made of.
examples: Wood is a strong material for building houses.

oewn-06648034-n.learner: facts, ideas, or things someone has noticed that can be used or worked into a finished piece of work.
examples: She gathered material for her book from old family letters.

oewn-03314753-n.learner: cloth made from natural or man-made threads by weaving, knitting, crocheting, or pressing them together (felting).
examples: She bought three metres of blue material to make a dress.

oewn-03735442-n.learner: the things you need to do or make something.
examples: Pens, paper, and other writing materials were laid out on the desk.

oewn-10320321-n.learner: a person who is thought good enough to be let into a place such as a school, or to be given a job.
examples: Her teachers agreed that she was university material.

connotation.why: rates a person as fit for a place or job, against plain 'candidate'

oewn-01813288-v.learner: to overcome someone completely, as a strong feeling or a strong sight, sound, or smell can.
examples: She was overpowered by shame and vexation.
the sight of such rooms, so many servants, and so splendid a dinner, might not wholly overpower them.

oewn-01112928-v.learner: to defeat someone by being stronger than they are.
examples: The guards overpowered the thief and took away his knife.

oewn-00011978-r.learner: in a bad, wrong, or unsatisfying way; not well.
examples: Elizabeth's congratulations were given with a sincerity, a warmth, a delight, which words could but poorly express.

oewn-02505278-v.learner: to give someone a penalty; to make someone suffer as a punishment.
examples: How shall we punish him for such a speech?
We can all plague and punish one another.

oewn-13960587-n.learner: the state of having been turned away or not accepted.
examples: Had he been a bad prig or a bad coxcomb, he might have been still smarting under his rejection

oewn-00204191-n.learner: the act of refusing to accept something.
examples: Her rejection of the old family customs surprised everyone.

oewn-07221933-n.learner: the act of saying that you will not accept something.
examples: I must, therefore, conclude that you are not serious in your rejection of me

oewn-11525736-n.learner: in medicine, the way the body's defence system refuses to accept substances or living things that it sees as foreign.
examples: The doctors gave him drugs to prevent rejection of his new kidney.

oewn-01020572-n.learner: the act of doing something again.
examples: Be not alarmed, madam, on receiving this letter, by the apprehension of its containing any repetition of those sentiments, or renewal of those offers

oewn-07356649-n.learner: something that happens again, in the same way as before.
examples: This year's flood was a repetition of the one we had last spring.

oewn-07113937-n.learner: the use of the same word or pattern of words again and again as a planned technique in speech or writing.
examples: The poet's repetition of the word 'never' gives the last line its power.

oewn-00912844-v.learner: to show or say that you are unhappy or not satisfied.
examples: One ought not to repine
Mrs. Bennet still continued to wonder and repine at his returning no more

connotation.why: discontent voiced as fretting, against plain 'complain'

oewn-02199359-v.learner: to fill someone with a feeling of dislike.
examples: She had even learnt to detect, in the very gentleness which had first delighted her, an affectation and a sameness to disgust and weary.

connotation.why: marks the thing as repellent, against plain 'displease'

oewn-01812341-v.learner: to cause strong dislike in someone, or to offend their sense of what is right.
examples: Everybody is disgusted with his pride.
Elizabeth was disgusted, and even Miss Bennet was shocked.

connotation.why: condemns the thing as morally offensive, against plain 'upset'

oewn-00980890-s.learner: making no stops that are not needed.
examples: We took the express train, so we reached the city in an hour.
